title: A grave in an old pit
date: c. AD 1 (late Iron Age, before the Roman conquest)
place: Llandough hill, above the River Ely
sources: media register MR-0096 / MR-0097 (Holbrook & Thomas 2005, 'An Early-medieval Monastic Cemetery at Llandough, Glamorgan: Excavations in 1994', Medieval Archaeology 49), p. 86 ('an iron-age burial?') and the B601 grave record

evidence_links.title: Holbrook & Thomas 2005, An Early-medieval Monastic Cemetery at Llandough, Glamorgan: Excavations in 1994 (PDF)

cast.IA_MOTHER: a late Iron Age woman about 45, grey-streaked dark hair in a long plait, plain undyed wool dress and a red-and-brown checked wool cloak pinned with a bronze brooch (invented)
cast.IA_SON: her son, about 20, fair-brown hair tied back, short beard stubble, plain brown wool tunic and trousers, leather belt (invented)

cast_rule: New faces; never the c. 200 BC roundhouse family of door 2, never a real family member.
setting: s10 (late Iron Age hill, north side, above the Ely)
dialogue_rule: A family's few words at a burial. The dead is a young adult; nothing else about them is known and nothing is invented (no name, no relation, no grave goods). No facts spoken beyond the record.

shots.direction: Grey late-autumn morning: the north crest of Llandough hill, the Ely marshes and river below in mist; very slow push-in.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 cinematic still, late Iron Age Britain c. AD 1. Wide landscape: the grassy north crest of a low inland hill in south-east Wales, below it a winding river through broad reed marshes and wet meadow under low mist, a grey late-autumn morning sky, a few bare hawthorns, a faint track. No text, no lettering, no heraldry or emblems, no modern objects, invented faces only, no likeness of any real person.
shots.motion: very slow push-in toward the hill crest; mist drifts across the marsh; reeds stir in light wind; no people

shots.direction: Mother and son carry a body wrapped in a checked wool cloak along the crest towards an old open pit; backs half to camera.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 cinematic still, late Iron Age Britain c. AD 1, grey morning. Medium-wide from behind and to one side: a late Iron Age woman about 45, grey-streaked dark hair in a long plait, plain undyed wool dress and a red-and-brown checked wool cloak pinned with a bronze brooch and her son, about 20, fair-brown hair tied back, short beard stubble, plain brown wool tunic and trousers, leather belt carry between them a body wrapped head to foot in a checked wool cloak along a grassy hill crest towards an old open pit with sloping sides cut in reddish clay; marsh mist far below. Faces turned away, no close faces. Respectful. No text, no lettering, no heraldry or emblems, no modern objects, invented faces only, no likeness of any real person.
shots.motion: the two walk slowly forward carrying the wrapped body, steady handheld follow, cloaks moving in the wind

shots.direction: IA_SON at the pit edge, three-quarters to camera, speaking to his mother off-frame; never to the lens.

lines.speaker: IA_SON
lines.en: The pit is already dug. We lay them here.
lines.cy: Mae'r pwll wedi'i dorri'n barod. Fan hyn y gosodwn ni nhw.
lines.es: El pozo ya está cavado. Acá los dejamos.

shots.direction: IA_MOTHER answers, eyes on the pit below her, three-quarters to camera.

lines.speaker: IA_MOTHER
lines.en: Gently, now. Cross the arms. Let them look up the slope.
lines.cy: Yn dyner, nawr. Croesa'r breichiau. Gad iddyn nhw edrych lan y llethr.
lines.es: Despacio, ahora. Cruzale los brazos. Que miren cuesta arriba.

shots.direction: High angle into the shallow pit: the wrapped body lies with the upper body on the pit's sloping side, arms crossed over the pelvis; dark hand-made potsherds in the clay spoil.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 cinematic still, late Iron Age Britain c. AD 1, grey morning light. High angle looking down into a shallow hollow cut in reddish clay on a grassy hill crest: a still figure fully wrapped and covered in a red-and-brown checked wool cloak lies peacefully as if asleep, the shoulders resting on the hollow's sloping side, the wrapped arms folded low across the body; a little heap of clay beside the hollow with a few dark hand-made pottery fragments in it; the hems of two people's wool clothes at the edge of frame. Quiet, tender, respectful. No text, no lettering, no heraldry or emblems, no modern objects, invented faces only, no likeness of any real person.
shots.motion: very slow overhead drift; a hand at frame edge smooths the cloak once; light wind moves grass at the rim

shots.direction: IA_SON kneeling by the pit, looking down, then to his mother off-frame.

lines.speaker: IA_SON
lines.en: So young. The wind is cold up here.
lines.cy: Mor ifanc. Mae'r gwynt yn oer fan hyn.
lines.es: Tan joven. Acá arriba el viento es frío.

shots.direction: IA_MOTHER lays a hand on her son's shoulder, speaks to him; never to the lens.

lines.speaker: IA_MOTHER
lines.en: Stay with me a while. Then we fill it in, together.
lines.cy: Aros gyda fi am sbel. Wedyn llenwn ni fe, gyda'n gilydd.
lines.es: Quedate conmigo un rato. Después lo llenamos, juntos.

shots.direction: Wide: the two stand side by side at the filled pit on the crest, backs to camera, looking out over the misty marsh; slow pull-back.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 cinematic still, late Iron Age Britain c. AD 1, late grey afternoon. Wide from behind: a late Iron Age woman about 45, grey-streaked dark hair in a long plait, plain undyed wool dress and a red-and-brown checked wool cloak pinned with a bronze brooch and her son, about 20, fair-brown hair tied back, short beard stubble, plain brown wool tunic and trousers, leather belt stand side by side on the grassy hill crest beside a low mound of freshly filled reddish earth, looking out over a winding river and misty reed marshes below; two wooden spades stuck upright in the earth. Backs to camera, no faces. No text, no lettering, no heraldry or emblems, no modern objects, invented faces only, no likeness of any real person.
shots.motion: slow pull-back and rise; the woman leans her head on her son's shoulder; mist drifts over the marsh

shots.direction: End card: title and date only.

language_rule: BIBLE PERIOD ACCURACY rule 4: the British language of the time is lost, so modern Welsh is spoken as its closest living descendant and the opening card states this once. Welsh and Spanish machine-written, for native review.
subtitles_rule: cy/en/es; Welsh cues start [in Welsh] in en/es; <=2x42 chars, <=20 cps, 0.83-7 s (subtitle_check.py)
no_fourth_wall: No narrator, no archivist, no modern frame; the mother and son speak only to each other.
render_status: cy prepared 2 Nov 2026 (stills, voices); renders first after 00:00Z 3 Nov under the scene-a-day rule (chrono_gate --render F002A first).
estate_location: Possible late Iron Age pit burial B601, 1994 excavation immediately north of the churchyard (MR-0097). ±50 m; overlap with Parcel A not checked
premise: Record: one possible late Iron Age grave, pit burial B601 (a young adult laid in a pit already dug, arms crossed on the pelvis), and 28 sherds of late Iron Age/early Roman pottery (16 in pit 805), found in the 1994 excavation immediately north of St Dochdwy's churchyard, on the ground Museum Wales records as 'Great House Farm, Llandough' (MR-0096, MR-0097). Overlap with Parcel A not checked.
